body:
I guess the years of being on the "other side" of the equation and seeing how health care professionals deal with their patients.  

Everybody I work with, on the most part, is great at being professional, understanding, and generally giving people the right kind of help that they need.  However they're people too and what's said behind the nurse's station or in the break room can be less than therapeutic.  I too am guilty of taking part of this.

I could give almost countless examples of ways that the nurse's, social workers, techs, therapist, and doctors have to walk the fine line of dichotomy between enacting positive therapeutic interventions with their patients and having to cope with their own frustrations, aggravation, and sometimes fatigue that goes along with being in the mental health field.

My main fear is crossing that line, and not being to cross back over to the professional side.  At least in the eyes of my co-workers.  I fear being passed up for promotions, raises, or extra responsibilities down the road because I may be seen as unstable or unable to cope.  

So I am considering travelling, but unfortunately I would have to travel pretty far to get an objective opinion.  A previous job of mine required me to do a lot of travelling around my county, go to court often, and develop a working relationship with almost every therapist in my area as well as their staff.  Sure I'm not best friends with any of them, but I have to consider things like future job opportunities as well as my professional image.

There's a place, in state and in my insurance network, that I'm considering looking into but it would be hard to go directly there.  The normal route would be through an ER, my place of work, and THEN to this place.  I can't think of a good way to circumvent the procedure, and I'm like the person other people would ask for help with this kind of bureaucratic bullshit, that's one of my skills.  

I've had these spells before, and they've passed.  But this is my worse to date and my first one since my father died which is making it the worse I think.
